newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM sees 1997 copper output at 433,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM sees 1997 copper output at 433,000 T.

text.p: Poland's KGHM copper concern expects to raise its copper output to 433,000 tonnes this year from 424,000 tonnes in 1996 and increase it to 470,000 tonnes in 1998, KGHM's deputy president Jerzy Dobrzanski said.

"We estimate that the world production of copper will be rising by 15 percent annually in the next few years so to maintain our market position we also intend to increase our production," Dobrzanski told a news conference.

He said KGHM also wanted to keep its leading position in world silver output by producing about 1,000 tonnes of silver annually -- flat at 1996 levels which gave it a seven percent share in global production.
"We want to maintain our silver output at current levels to keep world leadership," Dobrzanski said.
He also said the company would either maintain, or slightly increase its gold production which was at 500 kg in 1996 in the coming years.
KGHM is slated for domestic and international markets in mid-1997, but the precise division of tranches to be offered in Poland and abroad is not yet known.
